The reaction sequence involves a Stork enamine reaction. Cyclohexanone reacts with piperidine (a secondary amine) in the presence of an acid catalyst to form an enamine. A mild acid like p-toluenesulfonic acid (TsOH) is favorable because it catalyzes enamine formation without fully protonating the amine; HCl would form an unreactive piperidinium salt. The enamine then undergoes Michael addition to acrylaldehyde, and the resulting iminium intermediate is hydrolyzed by H₃O⁺ to yield the 2-substituted cyclohexanone, 3-(2-oxocyclohexyl)propanal.
